text:
maya: Heads-up: scheduling a midweek maintenance for apac-west1 WED 23:00-01:00 UTC. Objective: NIC microcode + nvlink driver patch across GPU racks. We'll do a staggered rack reboot in 4 cohorts to avoid a large capacity hit. Expected per-cohort draining window ~60m. Estimated temporary capacity dip ~10-15% while cohort is rebooting.

alex: SGTM. Which pools are we touching? any priority tenants that must be excluded?

maya: Affected pools = tag: apac-gpu-general and apac-gpu-spot-burst. We'll exclude pools tagged tenant-priority and reserved-dedicated. Priority customers list: tenant-retail-x, tenant-health-y — ops has been notified.

sam: Can you drop the runbook link here and the exact drain commands so oncall can copy?

maya: Runbook: https://redwood.internal/runbooks/apac-midweek-maint — main steps below.

maya: ```
# cordon + drain (graceful, keep pods with PDBs healthy)
kubectl cordon gpu-node-123
kubectl drain gpu-node-123 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --grace-period=120
# wait for evictions + verify
kubectl get pods -o wide --field-selector spec.nodeName=gpu-node-123
```

natalie: Are we pre-seeding KV cache / prefix cache on canaries to avoid cold token latencies?

alex: Yes, plan is: canary cohort (2 nodes) -> reboot -> run kv-seed job 10m after node ready -> smoke tests -> then proceed. I'll run an extra manual seed for the first canary.

maya: autoscripts will run kv-seed 15m post-boot, but manual seed for canary as alex said. Also will keep one control-plane replica in-region for routing checks.

tony: Quick cost question: will cross-region failover for some requests spike egress or burst capacity charges? Need an estimate to flag to finance.

maya: Minimal — we estimate ~2% added cost for the 2h window due to fallback to us-west and eu pools. Finance already reviewed and OK. Linked details: https://redwood.internal/ops/maint-costs/apac-2026-03

sam: Can we add a console banner and customer-facing notice for tenants above threshold?

maya: Yes — I'll post a console banner 2h before and send an outbound notice to customers with SLA-impact risk >= medium. Draft for review: "Planned maintenance in APAC tonight; brief latency increases possible for some hosted requests. No data loss expected."

alex: Monitoring/checklist:
- preflight: verify canary seed passed
- during: watch p50/p95 latency + token TPS, queue depth
- post: KV hit-rate, cold-start ratio, rollback if latency >SLO for >10m

natalie: Can we set automated rollback if p95 doubles for more than 5m?

maya: Yes — set policy in the rollout: auto-pause + rollback if p95 > 2x baseline for 5m. I've added a tracing hook to the canary routes.

infra-bot: scheduled-maintenance-bot: Maintenance ticket created: #MNT-7832. Cohorts: a,b,c,d. Canaries: gpu-node-101, gpu-node-102. ETA: 2h window.

alex: I'll own canary execution and post results in this thread. Sam, can you update the ops-runbook with the warmup commands we used last quarter?

sam: On it, will push updates in 10m and ping #customer-ops for the notice.

tony: Thx — finance wants a follow-up summary with actual cost delta after the window.

maya: Will post a post-maint cost + impact summary here within 24h. :thumbsup:

alex: Canaries started at 23:05 UTC, kv-seed triggered at 23:16, smoke tests green. Proceeding to cohort A drain at 23:30.

sam: Noted. I'll keep an eye on alerting and paging.

natalie: Observability note: ramp down sampling to keep traces within quota during the window.

maya: Good call. Lowered trace sampling to 5% for apac routes for the maintenance window.

alex: Cohort A reprovisioned + back in pool at 23:58, latency within expected bounds. Moving to cohort B now.

maya: Thanks team. Please update the ticket with any anomalies. If anything looks off, invoke rollback plan immediately.

infra-bot: scheduled-maintenance-bot: Cohort A completed, duration 28m. No rollback.

sam: Great — will post a short customer postmortem-style note after all cohorts finish.

maya: End-of-thread summary: maintenance completed across 4 cohorts by 00:45 UTC. Peak cross-region traffic ~1.8% above baseline, cost delta ~1.9%, no customer SLA breaches. Full writeup in #ops-postmortems.
